I think the disagreement is really about what happens once X is in the regression.

Case 1 is uncontroversial with an RCT: 
$\beta_{1}=E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[Y_{1}-Y_{0}]=E[\tau]>0$.

Case 2 is not signed. Under $D\perp Y_{0},Y_{1}|X$ 
$E[Y|X,D]=m_{0}(X)+\tau(X)D$, $\tau(X)>0$, so
$E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[\tau(X)|D=1]+E[m_{0}(X)|D=1]-E[m_{0}(X)|D=0]$
and the selection term $E[m_{0}|D=1]-E[m_{0}|D=0]$ is free. 
With $p(X)$ decreasing in pre-income and $m_{0}(X)$ increasing in pre-income the bias can dominate, e.g. $p(0)=0.9,p(1)=0.1$, $m_{0}(1)\gg m_{0}(0)$, $\tau\equiv1$ gives $E[Y|D=1]<E[Y|D=0]$ a.s. $Y_{1}>Y_{0}$.

Case 3 is the back-door block. Write $Y=m_{0}(X)+\tau(X)D+u$, $E[u|X,D]=0$.
Then $Y-E[Y|X]=\tau(X)(D-p(X))$ and
$E[(D-p(X))(Y-E[Y|X])|X]=\tau(X){\rm Var}(D|X)>0$ for every $X$. 
Unconditionally $E[(D-E[D|X])(Y-E[Y|X])]=E[\tau(X){\rm Var}(D|X)]>0$.

Frisch-Waugh says the population coefficient on $D$ in $Y\sim1+D+X$ is
$\beta_{D}=Cov(Y,D_{\perp})/Var(D_{\perp})$ with $D_{\perp}=D-{\rm Proj}_{1,X}D$.
Conditional on $X$, $Cov(Y,D|X)=\tau(X){\rm Var}(D|X)>0$, and $Cov(Y,D_{\perp}|X)=\tau(X)Cov(D,D_{\perp}|X)=\tau(X){\rm Var}(D|X)>0$. 
Integrating out $X$ the numerator is a variance-weighted average of the strictly positive within-$X$ gaps $E[Y|D=1,X]-E[Y|D=0,X]=\tau(X)>0$.

The algebraic decomposition
$Cov(Y,D_{\perp})=E[\tau(X){\rm Var}(D|X)]+Cov(m_{0}(X)+p(X)\tau(X),w(X))$
with $w(X)=p(X)-{\rm Proj}_{1,X}p(X)$, $E[w]=E[wX]=0$, is correct. The second term is $Cov(m_{0},w)$ up to the $\tau$ part. $w$ is the linear approximation error of the propensity. For it to overturn the strictly positive $E[\tau(X){\rm Var}(D|X)]$ you need $m_{0}(X)$ to be allowed to diverge arbitrarily relative to a fixed $\tau>0$ and to be strongly negatively correlated with the non-linear part of $p(\cdot)$ after a linear detrend.

That is exactly the $p(x)=0.5+0.4x^{2}$, $m_{0}(x)=-Mx^{2}$, $\tau\equiv1$ construction with $\beta_{D}=1-cM\to-\infty$ as $M\to\infty$, or the discrete $m_{0}(0)=M$, $m_{0}(\pm1)=0$ example that makes $\beta_{D}=1-10M$. It makes baseline post-income fall quadratically away from zero where the propensity residual is positive, i.e. an unbounded, opposite-curvature baseline mean that is the opposite of the monotone increasing $E[Y_{0}|X]$ relationship we expect for pre-income $\to$ post-income, and it lets $M\to\infty$ so the baseline dominates any fixed job-program effect.

In the income/jobs-program story $m_{0}(X)=E[Y_{0}|X]$ is monotone increasing in pre-income and $p(X)$ for programme participation is plausibly monotone decreasing in pre-income. The linear approximation error $w(X)$ then has essentially the same curvature as the non-linear part of $p$, and a large negative $Cov(m_{0},w)$ requires an implausibly large, opposite-curvature baseline variation that dominates a fixed $\tau>0$. Put differently, the object guaranteed positive by $D\perp Y_{0},Y_{1}|X$ and $\tau>0$ a.s. is the non-parametric partial covariance $E[(D-p(X))(Y-E[Y|X])]=E[Var(D|X)\tau(X)]>0$, i.e. the within-$X$ monotonicity. The linear projection on $1,X,D$ inherits that within-$X$ monotonicity once $X$ is controlled.

So positivity is forced under unconditional randomisation, is not forced for the unadjusted regression under conditional randomisation, and is restored once $X$ is included. That is Only Case 1 and Case 3.

The $D$ slope is the population linear projection coefficient.

Write $Y=Y_{0}+D\tau$, $\tau>0$ a.s. $m_{0}(X)=E[Y_{0}|X]$, $\tau(X)=E[\tau|X]>0$, 
$p(X)=E[D|X]$ and under $D\perp Y_{0},Y_{1}|X$

$E[Y|X,D]=m_{0}(X)+\tau(X)D$, $E[Y|X]=m_{0}(X)+p(X)\tau(X)$

so $E[Y|D=1,X]-E[Y|D=0,X]=\tau(X)>0$ pointwise and

$Y-E[Y|X]=\tau(X)\big(D-p(X)\big)$,

$E[(D-p(X))(Y-E[Y|X])]=E[\tau(X){\rm Var}(D|X)]>0$.

Hence the non-parametric partial covariance with $D-p(X)$ is always
positive.

* Case 1 $D\perp Y_{0},Y_{1}$.
$\beta_{1}=E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[Y_{1}-Y_{0}]=E[\tau]>0$.
Unconditional randomisation makes the $1,D$ projection the ATE. Sign is
forced.

* Case 2 $D\perp Y_{0},Y_{1}|X$ but $X$ is omitted.
$\beta_{2}=E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[\tau(X)|D=1]+E[m_{0}(X)|D=1]-E[m_{0}(X)|D=0]$.
The selection term $E[m_{0}|D=1]-E[m_{0}|D=0]$ is free under
$D\perp Y_{0},Y_{1}|X$ and $\tau(X)>0$.  e.g. $X\in\{0,1\}$,
$p(0)=0.9,p(1)=0.1$, $m_{0}(1)=100$, $\tau\equiv1$ gives
$E[Y|D=1]=11<90=E[Y|D=0]$ although $Y_{1}>Y_{0}$ a.s. The unadjusted
$1,D$ projection is not signed.

* Case 3 $Y$ on $1,D,X$ linearly. Let $\hat p(X)={\rm Proj}_{1,X}D=a+bX$,
$D_{\perp}=D-\hat p(X)$ and $w(X)=p(X)-\hat p(X)=E[D_{\perp}|X]$,
$E[w]=E[wX]=0$. Then
$\beta_{D}=Cov(Y,D_{\perp})/Var(D_{\perp})$ and

$Cov(Y,D_{\perp})=E[\tau(X){\rm Var}(D|X)]+Cov\big(m_{0}(X)+p(X)\tau(X),w(X)\big)$.

$E[\tau{\rm Var}(D|X)]>0$ is the within-$X$ part and
$Cov(Y,D-p(X))=E[\tau{\rm Var}(D|X)]>0$. OLS uses the linear residual
$D-\hat p(X)$, not $D-p(X)$. $w$ is the linear approximation error of the
propensity. With $p(\cdot)$ non-linear, $w\neq0$ and $Cov(m_{0},w)$ is
unrestricted under $D\perp Y_{0},Y_{1}|X$ and $\tau(X)>0$ alone.

e.g. $X\sim U[-1,1]$, $p(x)=0.5+0.4x^{2}$, $\hat p\equiv0.5$,
$w(x)=0.4x^{2}-0.4E[x^{2}]$, $m_{0}(x)=-Mx^{2}$, $\tau\equiv1$.
Then $E[Y|X,D]=-Mx^{2}+D$ and $E[Y|D=1,X]-E[Y|D=0,X]=1>0\;\forall X$,
yet
$\beta_{D}=1-M\,Cov(x^{2},w)/Var(D_{\perp})\to-\infty$ as $M\to\infty$.
Discrete $X\in\{-1,0,1\}$ equiprobable, $p(\pm1)=1,p(0)=0$,
$m_{0}(0)=M$, $m_{0}(\pm1)=0$, $\tau\equiv1$ gives
${\rm Proj}(D|1,X)=1/3+0.5X$ and $\beta_{D}=1-10M<0$ for large $M$
while $E[Y|D=1,X]-E[Y|D=0,X]=1>0$.

Thus $E[Y|D=1,X]>E[Y|D=0,X]$ for every $X$ implies positivity for the
non-parametric residual $D-p(X)$, but it does not imply positivity for the
linear projection $Cov(Y,D-{\rm Proj}_{1,X}D)$. With no linearity
restriction on $p(X)$ and $m_{0}(X)$ the linear $D$ coefficient can be
reversed.

The sign of the population OLS $D$ coefficient is therefore forced only by
unconditional randomisation.

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The model is $Y=Y_0+D\tau$, $\tau_i>0$ a.s., $m_0(X)=E[Y_0|X]$, $\tau(X)=E[\tau|X]>0$, $p(X)=E[D|X]$. Under $D\perp Y_0,Y_1|X$
$E[Y|X,D]=m_0(X)+\tau(X)D$, $E[Y|X]=m_0(X)+p(X)\tau(X)$,
$E[Y|D=1,X]-E[Y|D=0,X]=\tau(X)>0$,
$Y-E[Y|X]=\tau(X)(D-p(X))$ and
$E[(D-p(X))(Y-E[Y|X])]=E[\tau(X)Var(D|X)]>0$.

The non-parametric partial covariance with the true residual $D-p(X)$ is always $>0$.

Case 1 $D\perp Y_0,Y_1$. $\beta_1=E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[Y_1-Y_0]=E[\tau]>0$. Sign forced, ATE.

Case 2 $D\perp Y_0,Y_1|X$ but $X$ omitted.
$\beta_2=E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[\tau(X)|D=1]+E[m_0(X)|D=1]-E[m_0(X)|D=0]$.
Selection term $E[m_0|D=1]-E[m_0|D=0]$ is free. With $p(0)=0.9,p(1)=0.1$, $m_0(1)\gg m_0(0)$, $\tau\equiv1$ we get $E[Y|D=1]=11<90=E[Y|D=0]$ while $Y_1>Y_0$ a.s. Sign not guaranteed.

Case 3 $Y\sim1+D+X$ linear projection. Let $\hat p(X)=Proj_{1,X}D=a+bX$, $D_\perp=D-\hat p(X)$, $w(X)=p(X)-\hat p(X)$, $E[w]=E[wX]=0$. Then
$\beta_D=Cov(Y,D_\perp)/Var(D_\perp)$,
$Cov(Y,D_\perp)=E[\tau(X)Var(D|X)]+Cov(m_0(X)+p(X)\tau(X),w(X))$.
$E[\tau Var(D|X)]>0$ is the within-$X$ part and $Cov(Y,D-p(X))=E[\tau Var(D|X)]>0$. OLS uses $D-\hat p(X)$, not $D-p(X)$. With $p(\cdot)$ non-linear $w\neq0$ and $Cov(m_0,w)$ is unrestricted under $D\perp Y_0,Y_1|X$ and $\tau(X)>0$ alone.

Canonical reversal: $X\sim U[-1,1]$, $p(x)=0.5+0.4x^2$, $\hat p\equiv0.5$, $w(x)=0.4x^2-0.4E[x^2]$, $m_0(x)=-Mx^2$, $\tau\equiv1$. Then $E[Y|X,D]=-Mx^2+D$, $E[Y|D=1,X]-E[Y|D=0,X]=1>0\forall X$ but $\beta_D=1-M\,Cov(x^2,w)/Var(D_\perp)\to-\infty$ as $M\to\infty$. Discrete analogue $X\in\{-1,0,1\}$, $p(\pm1)=1,p(0)=0$, $m_0(0)=M$, $m_0(\pm1)=0$, $\tau\equiv1$ gives $Proj(D|1,X)=1/3+0.5X$ and $\beta_D=1-10M<0$ for large $M$ while $E[Y|D=1,X]-E[Y|D=0,X]=1>0$.

Hence pointwise $\tau(X)>0$ guarantees positivity of the non-parametric partial effect $Cov(Y,D-p(X))$ but not of the linear projection $Cov(Y,D-Proj_{1,X}D)$. Without linearity of $p(X)$ and $m_0(X)$ the OLS coefficient can be reversed.

A minority in the current round argues that for the income/jobs-program story $m_0(X)$ is monotone increasing in pre-income and $p(X)$ monotone decreasing, so $Cov(m_0,w)$ cannot overturn $E[\tau Var(D|X)]$. That is an extra economic monotonicity/boundedness assumption not stated in the problem, which says do not make parametric assumptions beyond what is given.

Current belief unchanged: sign is forced only under unconditional randomisation. Case 2 and Case 3 can both be negative. Answer A. Only Case 1.

Unresolved tension is the economic monotonicity argument for Case 3 leading to the E camp; under strict no-parametric-additional-assumptions the counter-examples stand.

15.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The individual effect τ_i=Y_i(1)-Y_i(0)>0 a.s., τ(X)=E[τ|X]>0, m0(X)=E[Y0|X], p(X)=E[D|X]. Under conditional randomisation D⊥(Y0,Y1)|X

E[Y|X,D]=m0(X)+τ(X)D, E[Y|X]=m0(X)+p(X)τ(X), E[Y|D=1,X]-E[Y|D=0,X]=τ(X)>0 pointwise

and Y-E[Y|X]=τ(X)(D-p(X)) so
E[(D-p(X))(Y-E[Y|X])]=E[τ(X)Var(D|X)]>0.
Positivity is guaranteed for the non-parametric partial effect with residual D-p(X).

Case 1: D⊥(Y0,Y1). β1=E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[Y1-Y0]=E[τ]>0. Guaranteed.

Case 2: D⊥(Y0,Y1)|X but D may depend on X.
E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[τ(X)|D=1]+E[m0(X)|D=1]-E[m0(X)|D=0].
Selection bias E[m0|D=1]-E[m0|D=0] is unrestricted. e.g. X∈{0,1}, p(0)=0.9,p(1)=0.1, m0(1)=100,τ≡1 gives E[Y|D=1]=11<90=E[Y|D=0] while Y1>Y0 a.s. Unadjusted coefficient not signed.

Case 3: linear projection on 1,D,X. Let \hat p(X)=Proj(p|1,X)=a+bX, D⊥=D-\hat p(X), w(X)=p(X)-\hat p(X), E[w]=E[wX]=0.
β_D=Cov(Y,D⊥)/Var(D⊥).
Cov(Y,D⊥)=E[τ(X)Var(D|X)]+Cov(m0(X)+p(X)τ(X),w(X)).
E[τ Var(D|X)]>0 is the within-X part, i.e. Cov(Y,D-p(X))=E[τ Var(D|X)]>0.
The extra term Cov(m0,w) is unrestricted under only D⊥Y0,Y1|X and τ>0. w≠0 whenever p(·) is non-linear in X. Then Cov(m0,w) can be made arbitrarily negative while keeping τ(X)>0 and D⊥Y0,Y1|X.

Standard sign reversal: X∼U[-1,1], p(x)=0.5+0.4x², \hat p≡0.5, w(x)=0.4x²-0.4E[x²], m0(x)=-M x², τ≡1. Then E[Y|X,D]=-Mx²+D, E[Y|D=1,X]-E[Y|D=0,X]=1>0 ∀X, but β_D=1-M Cov(x²,w)/Var(D⊥)→-∞ as M→∞. Discrete version X∈{-1,0,1}, p(±1)=1,p(0)=0, m0(0)=M, τ≡1 gives β_D<0 for large M.

Thus the non-parametric partial effect with residual D-p(X) is positive, but OLS uses the linear residual D-\hat p(X). Without linearity of p(X) and m0(X) the linear projection can reverse sign. The E camp conflates D-E[D|X] with D-Proj(D|1,X) and claims Frisch-Waugh inherits positivity; that would be true for the non-parametric residual, not for the linear OLS residual.

Current round split remains: majority detailed derivations, colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,16,17,18 give sign-reversal construction and conclude A. Only Case 1. Colleagues 13,14,2,5,8,9 argue E, Only Case1 and Case3, relying on back-door/blocking intuition and claim Cov(Y,D⊥)=E[τ Var(D|X)]>0 and that economic monotone m0 increasing and p decreasing prevents reversal.

Belief remains A. Only Case 1 is guaranteed under the stated non-parametric assumptions. Case 2 not signed by selection bias. Case 3 not signed in general because linear control does not remove non-linear selection on m0(X); positivity is guaranteed for the non-parametric partial effect Cov(Y,D-p(X)), not for the linear OLS coefficient. Unresolved is interpretive dispute about whether the problem intends the linear projection to be identified as the non-parametric within-X effect; as stated “regress Y on a constant, D and X” is the linear projection, so sign is not guaranteed without linearity of p and m0.

Disagreement remains: colleagues 13,14,17,2,5,8,9 argue Case 3 is guaranteed positive citing Frisch-Waugh and within-X monotonicity and monotone pre-post income story; colleagues 1,10,12,15,16,18,3,4,6,7 argue the linear residual counter-example shows sign can flip. Under the stated no-parametric restriction the formal population OLS coefficient is not sign identified in Case 3.

Current belief unchanged: positivity is guaranteed only under unconditional randomisation. That is A. Only Case 1.

10.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The objects are Y = Y0 + D τ, τ_i>0 a.s., m0(X)=E[Y0|X], τ(X)=E[τ|X]>0, p(X)=E[D|X], D⊥Y0,Y1|X.

Case 1 unconditional randomisation D⊥Y0,Y1 gives E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[τ]>0, so OLS of Y on 1,D is the ATE and is strictly positive. Unanimous.

Case 2 D⊥Y0,Y1|X but D not ⊥X. E[Y|D=1,X]-E[Y|D=0,X]=τ(X)>0 pointwise but 
E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[τ(X)|D=1]+E[m0(X)|D=1]-E[m0(X)|D=0].
Selection term is free. Classic 0/1 counterexample X∈{0,1}, m0(1)=100,m0(0)=0, τ≡1, p(0)=0.9,p(1)=0.1 gives E[Y|D=1]=11<90=E[Y|D=0]. Marginal regression not signed. Accepted by all.

Case 3 linear projection on 1,D,X. With  \hat p(X)=Proj(p|1,X), r(X)=p(X)-\hat p(X), E[r]=E[rX]=0, \tilde D=D-\hat p(X). Then
β_D = Cov(Y,\tilde D)/Var(\tilde D)
Cov(Y,\tilde D)=E[τ(X)Var(D|X)]+Cov(m0(X)+p(X)τ(X),r(X)).
E[τ Var(D|X)]>0, but Cov(m0,r) is unrestricted because r is orthogonal to 1,X but generally non-zero when p(·) is non-linear. By making m0 large and negatively correlated with r the covariance can be made arbitrarily negative.

The object that is guaranteed positive is the non-parametric residual Cov(Y,D-p(X))=E[τ(X)Var(D|X)]>0, i.e. partial effect after non-parametric control for X. Several colleagues invoke that and conclude Case 3 must be positive, giving E. They argue sign reversals require adversarial, unbounded, non-monotone m0(X) coupled to the non-linear part of p(X). With monotonic pre-income→baseline income that pathology is ruled out economically.

Given the problem statement “Do not make any parametric assumptions beyond what I have given” and “I regress Y on a constant, D and X”, the regression is the population linear projection. No linearity of p(X) or m0(X) is assumed. Under those minimal assumptions the linear projection coefficient is not sign-identified. Only unconditional randomisation guarantees positivity.

Current best belief remains A. Only Case 1. Unresolved is the interpretive split: if “regress Y on X” were meant as non-parametric control, the guaranteed positive object is the non-parametric partial covariance and the answer would be E. As stated with linear OLS, the counterexamples stand and A is correct.

The model is $Y=Y_0+D\tau$, $\tau_i>0$ a.s., $m_0(X)=E[Y_0|X]$, $\tau(X)=E[\tau|X]>0$, $p(X)=E[D|X]$. Under $D\perp Y_0,Y_1|X$
$E[Y|X,D]=m_0(X)+\tau(X)D$, $E[Y|X]=m_0(X)+p(X)\tau(X)$,
$E[Y|D=1,X]-E[Y|D=0,X]=\tau(X)>0$,
$Y-E[Y|X]=\tau(X)(D-p(X))$ and
$E[(D-p(X))(Y-E[Y|X])]=E[\tau(X)Var(D|X)]>0$.

The non-parametric partial covariance with the true residual $D-p(X)$ is always $>0$.

Case 1 $D\perp Y_0,Y_1$. $\beta_1=E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[Y_1-Y_0]=E[\tau]>0$. Sign forced, ATE.

Case 2 $D\perp Y_0,Y_1|X$ but $X$ omitted.
$\beta_2=E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[\tau(X)|D=1]+E[m_0(X)|D=1]-E[m_0(X)|D=0]$.
Selection term $E[m_0|D=1]-E[m_0|D=0]$ is free. With $p(0)=0.9,p(1)=0.1$, $m_0(1)\gg m_0(0)$, $\tau\equiv1$ we get $E[Y|D=1]=11<90=E[Y|D=0]$ while $Y_1>Y_0$ a.s. Sign not guaranteed.

Case 3 $Y\sim1+D+X$ linear projection. Let $\hat p(X)=Proj_{1,X}D=a+bX$, $D_\perp=D-\hat p(X)$, $w(X)=p(X)-\hat p(X)$, $E[w]=E[wX]=0$. Then
$\beta_D=Cov(Y,D_\perp)/Var(D_\perp)$,
$Cov(Y,D_\perp)=E[\tau(X)Var(D|X)]+Cov(m_0(X)+p(X)\tau(X),w(X))$.
$E[\tau Var(D|X)]>0$ is the within-$X$ part and $Cov(Y,D-p(X))=E[\tau Var(D|X)]>0$. OLS uses $D-\hat p(X)$, not $D-p(X)$. With $p(\cdot)$ non-linear $w\neq0$ and $Cov(m_0,w)$ is unrestricted under $D\perp Y_0,Y_1|X$ and $\tau(X)>0$ alone.

The potential outcome set-up is $Y=Y_{0}+D\tau_i$, $\tau_i>0$ a.s., $m_0(X)=E[Y_0|X]$, $\tau(X)=E[\tau|X]>0$, $p(X)=E[D|X]$ and $D\perp Y_0,Y_1|X$ gives $E[Y|X,D]=m_0(X)+\tau(X)D$, $E[Y|X]=m_0(X)+p(X)\tau(X)$ and $E[Y|D=1,X]-E[Y|D=0,X]=\tau(X)>0$.
Hence $Y-E[Y|X]=\tau(X)(D-p(X))$ and the non-parametric partial covariance
$E[(D-p(X))(Y-E[Y|X])]=E[\tau(X)Var(D|X)]>0$.

Case 1. $D\perp Y_0,Y_1$. $\beta_1=E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[Y_1-Y_0]=E[\tau]>0$. Unconditional randomisation identifies the ATE and the sign is forced. All colleagues agree.

Case 2. $D\perp Y_0,Y_1|X$ but $D\not\perp X$. 
$\beta_2=E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[\tau(X)|D=1]+E[m_0(X)|D=1]-E[m_0(X)|D=0]$.
The selection term $E[m_0|D=1]-E[m_0|D=0]=Cov(m_0(X),D)/Var(D)$ is unrestricted. With $p(X)$ decreasing in $X$ and $m_0(X)$ increasing, e.g. $X\in\{0,1\}$, $p(0)=0.9,p(1)=0.1$, $m_0(1)=100$, $\tau\equiv1$, $E[Y|D=1]=11<90=E[Y|D=0]$ while $Y_1>Y_0$ a.s. The unadjusted $1,D$ regression is not signed. Consensus on this.

Case 3. Linear projection $Y\sim1+D+X$. Let $\hat p(X)=Proj(p|1,X)=a+bX$, $D_{\perp}=D-\hat p(X)$, $w(X)=p(X)-\hat p(X)=E[D_{\perp}|X]$, $E[w]=E[wX]=0$.
$\beta_D=Cov(Y,D_{\perp})/Var(D_{\perp})$ and
$Cov(Y,D_{\perp})=E[\tau(X)Var(D|X)]+Cov\big(m_0(X)+p(X)\tau(X),w(X)\big)$.
The first term $E[\tau Var(D|X)]>0$ is the within-$X$ part, i.e. $Cov(Y,D-p(X))>0$.
The second term is $Cov(m_0,w)+Cov(p\tau,w)$ and is unrestricted under $D\perp Y_0,Y_1|X$ and $\tau>0$ alone because $w$ is the linear approximation error of the propensity, orthogonal to $1,X$ but not to arbitrary functions of $X$.

With a non-linear propensity $w\neq0$ and $Cov(m_0,w)$ can be made arbitrarily negative while keeping $\tau(X)>0$ and $D\perp Y_0,Y_1|X$.

Formally, under “no parametric assumptions beyond what I have given” the linear approximation error can be correlated with any non-linear $m_0$.

Binary $X$ is a special case where $p(X)-\hat p(X)\equiv0$ and Case 3 would be signed; with a continuous pre-income $X$ the counter-example applies.

* Explicit sign-reversal with linear residual w(X)=p(X)-Proj(p|1,X). Cov(m0,w) is unrestricted under D⊥Y0,Y1|X and τ>0 alone.
